notes: Member names are case-sensitive and appear exactly as the schemas define them (snake_case). This hit keeps every required member in snake_case but emits three optional members in camelCase, which is what a Protocol Buffers JSON printer does by default. ServiceSearchResult allows additional properties for extensibility, so the instance is schema-valid. It still does not conform: durationMinutes, lastIndexedAt, and rankSignals are unrecognized members, not aliases of duration_minutes, last_indexed_at, and rank_signals. A consumer reading the defined names sees no duration, no freshness timestamp, and no availability ranking.

variants.case: every member camelCased, as the default Protocol Buffers JSON mapping emits
variants.why: Here schema validation does catch the defect, but only because service_id, service_name, category_ids, profile_url, and deployment_mode are required. The primary case shows the same defect on optional members passing the schema.

variants.case: the same hit with every member named as defined
variants.why: Control case: the checker's member-name scan must not flag a conforming instance.

wrong_answers.behaviour: treat schema validation as sufficient proof of conformance
wrong_answers.why: The primary instance passes the ServiceSearchResult schema. A registry tested only by schema validation ships camelCase optional members, and clients silently lose duration, freshness, and rank_signals.

wrong_answers.behaviour: emit JSON with the default Protocol Buffers printer
wrong_answers.why: The default mapping converts field names to lowerCamelCase. The variant shows the result: every required snake_case member is missing and the response fails validation.

wrong_answers.behaviour: consumer accepts serviceId as an alias for service_id
wrong_answers.why: Lenient aliasing hides a non-conforming producer from its tests while other consumers that read only the defined names break against it.
